class.name: CameraRig3D
class.brief_description: A 3D camera rig that follows a target, smoothly adjusts its position, and keeps its camera pointed at the target.
class.description: CameraRig3D is a camera controller that manages a Camera3D node to provide target following, position smoothing, automatic look-at behavior, and optional mouse orbit controls. The rig can create its own Camera3D child or adopt an existing Camera3D in its hierarchy, depending on [member adopt_existing_camera]. The managed camera is made current when the rig is initialized. The [member target] property specifies the Node3D that the rig follows and looks at. The [member follow_offset] property defines the desired position relative to the target. When position smoothing is enabled, the rig moves towards this position gradually instead of snapping to it. When [member mouse_orbit_enabled] is enabled, captured mouse movement rotates the follow offset around the target. The [member mouse_orbit_sensitivity], [member mouse_orbit_pitch_min], and [member mouse_orbit_pitch_max] properties control the orbit sensitivity and vertical rotation limits. The [method get_mouse_orbit_yaw] method returns the current horizontal orbit angle, which can be used for camera-relative movement. CameraRig3D can be used for third-person cameras and other camera setups. Nodes such as [SpringArm3D] can be used to handle camera collision.

method.name: get_mouse_orbit_yaw
method.description: Returns the current horizontal mouse orbit angle in radians. This can be used to make character movement relative to the camera's horizontal orientation.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the rig searches for an existing [Camera3D] in its hierarchy instead of creating a new camera. Cameras inside nested viewports are ignored.

The desired position offset from the target, expressed in the target's local space. The offset is transformed by the target's global transform. When mouse orbit is enabled, the offset's Z component determines the orbit distance, while its X and Y components remain positional offsets.
If [code]true[/code], the rig follows the target using [member follow_offset].
If [code]true[/code], the managed camera points towards the target.
If [code]true[/code], captured mouse movement rotates the follow offset around the target. Mouse input is ignored while the mouse is not captured.
The maximum vertical orbit angle in radians.
The minimum vertical orbit angle in radians.
Scales mouse movement when calculating horizontal and vertical orbit angles. Higher values make the camera orbit faster.

If [code]true[/code], the rig smoothly interpolates towards its desired position after initialization. Otherwise, it moves directly to the desired position. [b]Note:[/b] During initialization, the rig is placed directly at the desired position.
Controls how quickly the rig approaches its desired position when [member position_smoothing_enabled] is enabled. Higher values make the rig follow more quickly.
The [Node3D] that the rig follows and looks at. If no target is assigned, target-following and look-at updates are not performed. Changing the target resets the mouse orbit angles.
